elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Vendor expressly agrees to defend Customer from and against third-party claims within the listed categories.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against covered third-party claims and resulting losses.
elements.evidence: Vendor expressly indemnifies Customer for resulting damages, losses, liabilities, costs, expenses, and reasonable attorneys' fees.

elements.element: Customer's Affiliates must receive the same Vendor defence and indemnity protection.
elements.evidence: The Vendor obligation expressly covers “Customer and its Affiliates.”

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity must cover third-party allegations that the Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual-property rights.
elements.evidence: Clause (a) covers allegations that the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any intellectual-property right.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Clause (b) expressly covers claims arising from Vendor's breach of Applicable Law.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Clause (c) covers only unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor. It does not cover other Vendor-caused data breaches, such as unauthorized loss, destruction, or alteration, unless they independently constitute a breach of Applicable Law.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Clause (d) expressly covers Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnity procedure must require the indemnified party to give notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: The indemnified party must give prompt written notice, with delayed notice relieving the indemnifying party only to the extent of material prejudice.

elements.element: The indemnity procedure must give the indemnifying party control of the defence.
elements.evidence: The indemnifying party controls the defence using counsel reasonably acceptable to the indemnified party.

elements.element: The indemnity procedure must require reasonable cooperation by the indemnified party.
elements.evidence: The indemnified party must provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.

elements.element: Customer must indemnify Vendor for third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content or materials.
elements.evidence: Customer indemnifies Vendor for third-party claims arising out of content or materials Customer provides to Vendor.

elements.element: Customer must indemnify Vendor for third-party claims arising from Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Customer indemnifies Vendor for third-party claims arising out of Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity obligations must be limited to Customer-provided content or materials and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: No other Customer indemnity trigger is created by the rendered language; Sections 19.5, 21.3, and 30.5 reference indemnities but do not create additional Customer indemnification duties.

elements.element: Vendor must provide an intellectual-property indemnity for third-party claims concerning the Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: The first indemnity paragraph requires Vendor to defend and indemnify Customer for third-party allegations that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual-property rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: The exclusion is phrased as applying to obligations under “Section 20.1(a),” but no provision is numbered Section 20.1(a) in the rendered clause. It is therefore not operatively and unambiguously tied to the IP indemnity; it is also limited to unauthorized Customer modifications.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by combinations with other items.
elements.evidence: Substantive combination language is present, including an absent-the-combination causation condition, but it applies only by reference to the unnumbered and undefined “Section 20.1(a).”

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by Vendor's compliance with Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Substantive language concerning Customer's written specifications is present, but it applies only by reference to the unnumbered and undefined “Section 20.1(a).”

elements.element: For an actual or reasonably likely covered IP claim, Vendor must have a remedy to procure Customer's continued use rights.
elements.evidence: A procure-right remedy is stated, but its trigger is a claim under the unnumbered and undefined “Section 20.1(a),” so it is not unambiguously connected to the operative IP indemnity.

elements.element: For an actual or reasonably likely covered IP claim, Vendor must have a remedy to modify the affected item so it is non-infringing.
elements.evidence: A functionally equivalent, non-infringing modification remedy is stated, but it depends on the unnumbered and undefined “Section 20.1(a).”

elements.element: For an actual or reasonably likely covered IP claim, Vendor must have a remedy to replace the affected item with a functionally equivalent non-infringing item.
elements.evidence: A functionally equivalent, non-infringing replacement remedy is stated, but it depends on the unnumbered and undefined “Section 20.1(a).”

elements.element: If the procure, modify, and replace remedies are not commercially feasible, Vendor must provide a refund remedy.
elements.evidence: The clause provides termination and refunds of prepaid fees and affected Deliverable fees if the other remedies are infeasible, but the remedy is triggered only through the unnumbered and undefined “Section 20.1(a).”

elements.element: Vendor's indemnification liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to 3× annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3× annual-fees cap appears. Section 21.3 instead classifies indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims, indicating they are carved out of the ordinary limitation regime rather than subjected to the required super-cap.

result.reason: The redline substantially implements the preferred indemnity, but its Vendor-caused data-incident trigger is narrower than the requested data-breach coverage. The fallback is independently unsatisfied because the required 3× annual-fees super-cap is absent; the exclusions and remedies also rely on a Section 20.1(a) reference that is not numbered or otherwise defined in the rendered operative text. The original unrelated provisions remain intact, but the redline is not minimal because it does not reach either complete level and adds additional related terms such as settlement restrictions, Customer defence duties, IP exclusions, and remedies.
